landscape.questionsSubheader: Simplify each expression — show your working in your workbook

intro.note: A letter stands for a number we do not know yet. Simplify each expression by collecting like terms. Show your working in your workbook.

visual.title: Visual aid — collecting like terms
visual.caption: Tiles of the same kind join together: 2x + 3 and x + 1 give 3x + 4.

params.aria: Algebra tiles: two x-tiles and three unit tiles, plus one x-tile and one unit tile, combine to make three x-tiles and four unit tiles.

methodSteps: 3  Add or subtract the number parts
commonMistakes: 3x means 3 × x. It is not the digits 3 and x written side by side.
You can only collect like terms: 3x + 2x = 5x, but 3x + 2 stays as 3x + 2.
x on its own means 1x, so x + x = 2x — not x².
Multiplying is different from adding: x × x = x², but x + x = 2x.
workedExample: Step 1 — Like terms:  2x and x are like;  3 and 1 are like.
Step 3 — Combine the x terms:  2x + x = 3x

A rectangle has length (x + 3) and width x. Write a simplified expression for its perimeter.

intro.objective: Understand that a letter stands for a number we do not know yet. Write simple expressions, simplify them by collecting like terms, and substitute a number for a letter to find a value.
commonMistakes: 3x means 3 × x. It is not the digits 3 and x written next to each other.
You can only collect like terms. For example 3x + 2x = 5x, but 3x + 2 stays as 3x + 2.
x on its own means 1x, so x + x = 2x — not x².
Multiplying is different from adding: x × x = x², but x + x = 2x.
methodSteps: Step 1: Find the like terms — the ones with the same letter (and the plain numbers together).
Step 2: Group the like terms, keeping the + or − sign in front of each one.
Step 3: Add or subtract the number parts (the coefficients) of each group.
Step 4: Write the simplified expression — letters first, then the number.
Step 5: Check by substituting a number for the letter.
workedExample: Step 1 — Find the like terms:  4x and 2x are like;  3 and −1 are like.

methodReminder: 3  Add or subtract the number parts

questions.content: Write an expression for a number, n, with 5 added to it.
frame: A letter, n, stands for the number you do not know yet.
"5 added to it" means you do +5 after the n.
Write the letter, then the operation, then the number.
Each a is one lot of a, so this is 1a + 1a + 1a + 1a.
Count how many a's there are altogether and write that number in front of the a.

questions.content:
A pencil costs p pence.

(a) Write an expression for the cost of 4 pencils and a 30p rubber.
(b) Work out the cost when p = 25.

A rectangle has length (x + 3) and width x.

(a) Write a simplified expression for its perimeter.
(b) Work out the perimeter when x = 4.
